name: usb-c-data
title: USB-C receptacle with USB 2.0 data, ESD protection, CC pull-downs and a polyfuse
about: USB-C receptacle for a USB 2.0 device: D+ and D− of both rows joined so that the plug works either way round (REQ.missing/usb_data), a USBLC6-2SC6 on D+/D− with its VBUS pin on the fused rail and 100 nF there, 5.1 kΩ on CC1 and on CC2 so that a USB-C host or charger switches VBUS on (REQ.missing:cc), and a 1.5 A polyfuse in VBUS. The data side of usb-c-sink.

ports.dp: USB D+ to the device (USB-UART, MCU)

accept.LIM.v: The drawing's 'voltage rating 5.0 V' is the USB rated voltage; USB-C vSafe5V allows 4.75–5.5 V and every USB-C receptacle works there. Dielectric withstanding voltage AC 100 V for 1 minute (drawing note 4-4).

components.label: {as}: ESD protection D+/D− and VBUS (USBLC6-2SC6)
components.notes: Flow-through: D+ through pins 1 and 6, D− through pins 3 and 4 (datasheet figure 18); VBUS pin 5 on the receptacle's VBUS with C1 – next to J1.

components.label: {as}: 100 nF at the USBLC6 VBUS pin

nets.name: vbus_in
nets.notes: VBUS at the receptacle, in front of the fuse, with the USBLC6-2's VBUS pin and its 100 nF.

accept.LIM.v: The USBLC6-2's VBUS pin: VRM 5.25 V is the voltage at which ST specifies the leakage (150 nA max, datasheet Rev 5, table 2); the transil from VBUS to GND breaks down at VBR ≥ 6 V (1 mA), so at USB-C's vSafe5V maximum of 5.5 V it does not clamp – only its leakage is unspecified there.

nets.name: dp
nets.notes: D+ of both rows (A6, B6) joined.

nets.name: dn
nets.notes: D− of both rows (A7, B7) joined.

notes: D+ (A6, B6) and D− (A7, B7) of both rows joined: a USB-C plug fits either way round and uses one row's pair (REQ.missing/usb_data).

CC: 5.1 kΩ from each CC pin to ground, one resistor per pin – the sink's Rd of the USB Type-C specification, without which a USB-C host or charger leaves VBUS off (REQ.missing:cc, REQ.value:cc 5.1 kΩ ± 10 %, REQ.forbidden:cc). Without a PD controller the source gives 5 V; the Rp it shows on CC (0.5, 1.5 or 3 A) is not read (HINT.usb_budget).

ESD: USBLC6-2SC6 (ST, Doc ID 11265 Rev 5) – for USB 2.0 up to 480 Mbit/s, 3.5 pF max per line, IEC 61000-4-2 level 4. Flow-through as its figure 18: D+ through pins 1 and 6, D− through pins 3 and 4; VBUS pin 5 on the receptacle's VBUS with 100 nF (CBUS, figure 18), as in its USB application figure 14 – in front of the fuse, as close to the connector as the layout allows (datasheet 2.3).
F1: 1.5 A polyfuse (as in usb-c-sink) – holds 1.5 A at 23 °C, 1.34 A at 40 °C, trips at 3 A; the receptacle is rated 3.0 A (drawing note 4-1). A USB 2.0 port gives 500 mA after configuration.
LIM.v is accepted twice with its reason: J1's voltage rating 5.0 V and the USBLC6-2's VRM 5.25 V against USB-C's 5.5 V (vSafe5V). On a USB 2.0 host (VBUS ≤ 5.25 V) neither applies.
No series resistors on D+/D− here – they belong to the device: a CH340C wants none (block esp32-wroom-32e), an RP2040 27 Ω per line (maker-coverage MCU 8). Route D+/D− as a pair (90 Ω differential).
Shell (EH) straight to GND; SBU1/SBU2 unused.
sim.json: the receptacle under sources (plus "A4B9", minus "A1B12") when it powers the board; a bulk capacitor behind F1 (HINT.bulk) – more than 10 µF directly on VBUS is HINT.usb_inrush.

test.about: SIG and SIG2 stand in for the D+/D− of a USB device (a USB-UART or an MCU), which the example lacks.
